name: M777 155mm Towed Howitzer
representative_system: M777A2 (BAE Systems), firing M795 / M982 Excalibur precision rounds

cost.display: ~$3.7M per gun (estimates range $2.5–4.4M depending on whether life-cycle costs are included); a single M982 Excalibur precision round runs ~$100K

key_facts.label: Max range
key_facts.value: ~40 km with M982 Excalibur precision rounds

short_role: Towed 155mm howitzer providing indirect fire support; titanium construction keeps it light enough for helicopter/vehicle relocation.
characteristics: Range: ~24-30 km with standard rounds, up to ~40 km with M982 Excalibur precision-guided rounds
Digital fire-control system for rapid self-location and laying (minutes to first round)
Positioned ~10-20 km from the line to stay within range while reducing counter-battery exposure
employment_notes: Rarely fires from a static position for long — 'shoot and scoot' displacement after a few fire missions is now standard, driven by counter-battery radar and reconnaissance drones that can locate a firing signature within minutes.
contrast_vs_traditional: Traditional artillery doctrine assumed relatively safe rear firing positions; today, persistent overhead drone reconnaissance and fast counter-battery radar mean a gun that fires from the same spot twice risks being hit within minutes. This has pushed batteries toward dispersion, frequent displacement, and much heavier reliance on drone-spotted precision rounds (like Excalibur) to reduce the number of shots — and therefore the exposure time — needed per target.

reactive_behavior.description: On select: crew lays the gun, fires, brief fall-of-shot indicator downrange toward zero line.

connections.description: Receives target coordinates and fall-of-shot correction from a tactical reconnaissance drone.
Crew casualties evacuated via the tactical casevac chain.
